title: Hardship Desk Q&A: Good-Faith Credit on the Deferral Fee
content:
**What is the good-faith credit?** A flat dollar credit subtracted from the deferral fee on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts. It follows the installments paid on the contract, counted as its scheduled-installment payments less its returned payments, and the partial payments posted on the request date.

| Installments paid | Partial payment posted on the request date | Good-faith credit |
|---|---|---|
| 12 or more | yes | seasoned good-faith deferral credit: 3.00 |
| fewer than 12 | yes | new good-faith deferral credit: 1.50 |
| any | none | no credit |

**Does a partial payment from an earlier day count?** No. Only a partial payment posted on the request date itself counts; one posted the day before does not.

**Does a scheduled-installment payment made today count?** No. The credit looks at partial payments.

**How are installments paid counted?** All scheduled-installment payments on the loan history, less all returned payments. Hypothetical: 14 scheduled-installment payments and 2 returned payments give 12, so a partial payment posted on the request date earns 3.00; 13 and 2 give 11, earning 1.50.

**A worked figure?** Hypothetical: a fee of 43.75 before credits, for a borrower with 20 installments paid and a partial payment posted on the request date, comes to 40.75 after this credit.
